seeds.scene: A cliff edge 10 m high with a person throwing a ball horizontally outward at moderate speed. A grid of 1m squares is overlaid for reference. Beside the cliff, three target buckets sit at ground level: bucket A is 4m from cliff base, bucket B is 7m out, bucket C is 12m out. The ball's initial horizontal velocity is 5 m/s (printed on a velocity gauge), gravity 9.8 m/s².
seeds.question: Into which bucket does the ball land?
seeds.lever: Compute time to fall: t = √(2h/g) = √(20/9.8) ≈ 1.43 s. Horizontal distance = 5 × 1.43 ≈ 7.14 m → bucket B (at 7m).

seeds.scene: A tall transparent jar holds three immiscible liquids in clear stratified layers (top to bottom): vegetable oil, water, honey. Five small objects float at various depths: a cork ball at the very top of oil; a plastic bead at the oil-water interface; a grape at the water-honey interface; a steel marble at the bottom of the honey; a wax cube floating between water and oil layers (interface).
seeds.question: Order the 5 objects by DENSITY from least dense to most dense.
seeds.answer: cork, wax, plastic bead, grape, steel marble
seeds.lever: Read floating depth as density indicator; objects sit at the interface where their density matches local fluid. Cork floats on top → least dense; steel sinks to bottom → most dense.

seeds.scene: A side view of a wrench applied to a hex bolt. Three force-arrows are drawn at different positions along the wrench handle: F1 at 5 cm from the bolt, magnitude 50 N. F2 at 15 cm, magnitude 30 N. F3 at 25 cm, magnitude 15 N. All three forces are perpendicular to the handle.
seeds.question: Which force produces the GREATEST torque on the bolt?

seeds.scene: Two ceramic cups sitting on a cool kitchen counter (room temp 20°C). Cup A held boiling water (98°C) and has been sitting for 30 minutes. Cup B held cold water (5°C) and has also been sitting for 30 minutes. The room is well-ventilated.
seeds.question: After enough time, which cup will be HOTTER?
seeds.answer: They will be the same temperature (room temp ~20°C)
seeds.lever: Reject the trap of 'A still hotter'; thermal equilibrium dictates both reach room temp.

seeds.scene: A Newton's cradle with 5 identical steel balls. The leftmost 2 balls are pulled back together and released. Question: predict what happens at the right side.
seeds.question: How many balls swing OUT on the right side after impact?
seeds.lever: Conservation of momentum + energy in equal-mass elastic collision; n balls in → n balls out.

seeds.scene: A diagram of a single-block-and-tackle pulley system: a fixed pulley at the top, a movable pulley supporting a 100 kg load, with one end of the rope attached to the ceiling and the other end pulled down by a person. Two segments of rope support the movable pulley.
seeds.question: How much force must the person apply to lift the load (ignoring friction)?
seeds.answer: Half the load weight ≈ 500 N (or 50 kg-force)
seeds.lever: Pulley mechanical advantage = number of supporting rope segments (2); force = weight / 2.

seeds.scene: Three identical 100mL water spills on the floor of three different rooms. Room A: warm (28°C), low humidity (30%), windy fan blowing. Room B: cool (18°C), high humidity (80%), still air. Room C: warm (28°C), high humidity (80%), still air. Surface area of each spill is the same.
seeds.question: Which spill EVAPORATES FASTEST?
seeds.lever: Evaporation favored by high temp + low humidity + airflow; A wins on all three.

seeds.scene: A ramp with adjustable angle. A crate sits on the ramp. The coefficient of static friction is μ=0.3 (printed on the ramp). The ramp angle indicator reads 20°.
seeds.question: Will the crate slide?
seeds.lever: Compare tan(angle) with μ_s; tan 20° ≈ 0.364 > μ = 0.3, so static friction is exceeded → crate slides.

seeds.scene: Three bar magnets laid out on a table with their N (red) and S (blue) poles labeled. Magnet 1: N-left, S-right. Magnet 2: S-left, N-right. Magnet 3: N-left, S-right. Each pair shown side by side with a small gap. Pair (1,2) faces N-S, Pair (2,3) faces N-N, Pair (1,3) faces S-N.
seeds.question: Which pairs ATTRACT each other?
seeds.lever: Determine the facing-pole pair for each adjacency. Pair (1,2): S of 1 meets S of 2 → repel. Pair (2,3): N of 2 meets N of 3 → repel. Pair (1,3): S of 1 meets N of 3 → attract.

seeds.scene: A ramp with two objects placed at the top: a solid metal cylinder (free to roll) and a flat metal block (sliding only). Both have the same mass. The ramp has very low friction (effectively frictionless for sliding). They are released simultaneously.
seeds.question: Which reaches the bottom FIRST?
seeds.lever: Rolling cylinder has rotational kinetic energy + translational; sliding block has only translational → all PE → translational KE → faster (assuming low friction).

seeds.scene: Three identical light bulbs labeled A, B, C arranged in a circuit: bulb A is in series with the parallel combination of B and C. The circuit is powered by a 9V battery.
seeds.question: Which bulb is the BRIGHTEST?
seeds.lever: Bulb A carries the full current; bulbs B and C share current (each gets half). Brightness scales with power = I²R; A has higher current.

seeds.scene: A row of 8 standing dominos. Domino 1 is leaning toward domino 2 by ~3°, the others are perfectly upright. Spacing between adjacent dominos is 4 cm; each domino is 5 cm tall and 2 cm wide. Domino 1 is given a slight push toward domino 2.
seeds.question: How many dominos will fall?
seeds.lever: Recognize the spacing (4cm) is less than domino height (5cm), so each falling domino reaches and topples the next.

seeds.scene: Two buckets connected by a hose forming a siphon. Bucket A (left) has water surface at height 60 cm. Bucket B (right) has water surface at height 40 cm. Hose loops over the top edge of both buckets. The siphon is primed (full of water).
seeds.question: Which direction does water flow?
seeds.answer: From A to B (higher to lower)
seeds.lever: Siphon flows toward lower water surface.

seeds.scene: A vertical pole 2 m tall casts a shadow on flat ground. The shadow length is 3.46 m. (For reference, tan 30° ≈ 0.577.)
seeds.question: What is the sun's elevation angle above the horizon?
seeds.lever: tan(angle) = pole_height / shadow_length = 2 / 3.46 ≈ 0.577 → angle = 30°.

seeds.scene: Top-down view of a ripple tank with two point wave sources S1 and S2 separated by 6 cm, oscillating in phase. Wavelength is 2 cm. A detector point P sits at distance 7 cm from S1 and 5 cm from S2.
seeds.question: Is the detector at a CONSTRUCTIVE or DESTRUCTIVE interference point?
seeds.lever: Path difference = 7-5 = 2 cm = 1λ → integer multiple of wavelength → constructive.

seeds.scene: A railway track has a 6 mm gap between two rail segments at 10°C ambient temperature. The rail is steel (linear expansion coefficient α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ /°C). One rail segment is 25 m long. Summer can reach 40°C.
seeds.question: By how much will one rail segment expand by summer? Will the gap close?
seeds.answer: Expansion ≈ 9 mm; gap will close (and rails would press)
seeds.lever: ΔL = α × L × ΔT = 1.2e-5 × 25000 mm × 30°C = 9 mm; 9 mm > 6 mm gap → closes.

seeds.scene: A balance beam pivoted at center. Left side: a 2 kg weight at 30 cm from pivot, AND a 1 kg weight at 50 cm from pivot. Right side: a 4 kg weight at unknown distance d.
seeds.question: What distance d on the right side balances the beam?
seeds.lever: Sum left moments: 2×30 + 1×50 = 110 kg·cm. Set equal to right: 4 × d = 110 → d = 27.5 cm.

seeds.scene: A tall water tank 5 m deep, with a small valve at the bottom. Pressure gauge at depth 2 m reads 20 kPa above atmospheric. Tank is open to air.
seeds.question: What does the pressure gauge at the BOTTOM (5 m depth) read above atmospheric?
seeds.lever: Pressure scales linearly with depth; 20 kPa at 2 m → 10 kPa per meter; at 5 m → 50 kPa.

seeds.scene: A figure skater spins on ice with arms extended outward, holding two heavy water bottles. The skater pulls arms inward (bottles brought close to body).
seeds.question: What happens to the spin RATE?
seeds.lever: Conservation of angular momentum L = Iω; reducing I (arms in) increases ω.

seeds.scene: A row of 5 dominos stands upright. Each domino is 5 cm tall, 2 cm wide. Spacing between consecutive dominos increases linearly: 3, 5, 7, 9 cm gaps. Domino 1 is pushed.
seeds.question: How many dominos fall in the chain?
seeds.lever: Each falling domino reaches the next only if gap < height. Gaps: 3<5 ✓ falls 2; 5=5 borderline could fall 3; 7>5 ✗. So D1→D2→D3→? ; D3 falls and arc reaches at most 5cm forward, gap to D4 is 7cm, fails. Total = 3 fall.
